title: the WSG encumbrance and movement - Table 11 (the encumbrance limits) and Table 12 (the character movement on foot)
audit_comment: The encumbrance and movement slice pins Table 11 (the 14 strength rows x the Light/Moderate/Heavy/Severe gp limits), Table 12 (the encumbrance category x the terrain class, the normal and the accelerated rates), the bulk rule-of-thumb, the terrain definitions and the large-scale overland movement rules (rules/wsgencum.h, prefix wem); census 356 -> 357.

banner.title: The WSG ENCUMBRANCE AND MOVEMENT, R432: Table 11 (the encumbrance limits for characters - the 14 strength rows x the Light/Moderate/Heavy/Severe ranges, each category begins at the previous one over) and Table 12 (the character movement on foot - the encumbrance category x the normal/rugged/very-rugged terrain class, the normal and the accelerated miles per half-day) with the bulk rule-of-thumb, the terrain definitions and the large-scale overland movement rules - the round opens the encumbrance-and-movement chapter. Census 356 -> 357.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed pp. 30-31; the user own copy OCR cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer and the IIIF eye-read; the disputed 18/01-50 severe cell read 1751-2500 at full resolution (the half-resolution vision 2250 was the artifact); every number matched.
banner.sentinel: The Table 11 light range begins at the light-column low number; each heavier category begins at the previous category over; below the light low number the character is not encumbered, above the severe high number he cannot move. Table 12 reads normal/accelerated miles per half-day for a base 12-inch character, scaled down for slower ones.

consts.name: wemGpPerPound
consts.comment: The standard conversion: a weight of 10 gp is one pound.

consts.name: wemBulkNonFactor
consts.comment: The rule of thumb: a non-bulky item rates its own weight in gp (equal to, or only slightly greater).

consts.name: wemBulkyFactorMin
consts.comment: A bulky object rates at least two times its weight.

consts.name: wemBulkyFactorMax
consts.comment: A bulky object rates two or three times its weight (the upper bound).

consts.name: wemVeryBulkyFactor
consts.comment: A very bulky object rates at least five times its weight.

consts.name: wemEncRowCount
consts.comment: The Table 11 strength-row count.

consts.name: wemPctRowBase
consts.comment: The first percentile row index in Table 11 (the 18/01-50 row).

consts.name: wemTerrainClassCount
consts.comment: The terrain classes for movement rate: normal, rugged, very rugged.

consts.name: wemSnowRuggedMinIn
consts.comment: Normal terrain under 5 to 10 inches of snow counts as rugged (the low bound).

consts.name: wemSnowRuggedMaxIn
consts.comment: Normal terrain under 5 to 10 inches of snow counts as rugged (the high bound).

consts.name: wemSnowVRuggedNormalIn
consts.comment: Normal terrain with more than 10 inches of snow counts as very rugged.

consts.name: wemSnowVRuggedRuggedIn
consts.comment: Rugged terrain with more than 5 inches of snow counts as very rugged.

consts.name: wemRuggedStreamMinHrs
consts.comment: Streams crossed one every 3-4 hours make the terrain rugged (the low bound).

consts.name: wemRuggedStreamMaxHrs
consts.comment: Streams crossed one every 3-4 hours make the terrain rugged (the high bound).

consts.name: wemVRuggedStreamHrs
consts.comment: Rivers or streams crossed one every 2 hours or less make the terrain very rugged.

consts.name: wemMilesPerInchHalfDay
consts.comment: Large-scale movement: each 1 inch of movement rate is that many miles per half-day.

consts.name: wemHalfDayHours
consts.comment: One half-day of movement is eight hours.

consts.name: wemRestHoursMin
consts.comment: A prolonged rest period is at least one hour.

consts.name: wemOver8hNum
consts.comment: Past eight hours without a prolonged rest: 3/4 of the normal maximum speed (numerator).

consts.name: wemOver8hDen
consts.comment: The past-eight-hours reduction denominator.

consts.name: wemOver16hNum
consts.comment: Past 16 hours without stopping to eat and rest: 1/3 of the normal maximum rate (numerator).

consts.name: wemOver16hDen
consts.comment: The past-16-hours reduction denominator.

consts.name: wemT12RowCount
consts.comment: The Table 12 encumbrance-category count.

consts.name: wemT12BaseMove
consts.comment: Table 12 assumes a base movement rate of 12 inches.

bools.name: wemOneSetClothingFree
bools.comment: One set of normal, light clothing adds no encumbrance.

bools.name: wemColdOuterwearCounts
bools.comment: Heavy and bulky cold-weather outerwear is not the free set of clothing.

bools.name: wemSoleSmallItemFree
bools.comment: Thieves' picks and tools, or any similar small item, add no encumbrance when carried alone.

bools.name: wemSmallComponentsFree
bools.comment: Material components for spells, when not large or bulky, add no encumbrance.

bools.name: wemHelmetWithArmorFree
bools.comment: A helmet (but not a great helmet) worn with armor adds no encumbrance.

bools.name: wemGreatHelmetCounts
bools.comment: A great helmet is not the free helmet.

bools.name: wemBulkMayExceedWeight
bools.comment: The bulk of an object may matter more than its weight (the 20-pound sack of feathers).

bools.name: wemEncValueDmRuling
bools.comment: The Dungeon Master frequently rules on the encumbrance value of objects.

bools.name: wemDeviationKeepProportions
bools.comment: Any DM deviation must keep the movement rates and the encumbrance limits in proportion to one another.

bools.name: wemBelowLightNotEncumbered
bools.comment: Below the light-column low number the character is not encumbered.

bools.name: wemAboveSevereCannotMove
bools.comment: Above the severe-column high number a character cannot move, engage in combat or perform any other physical activity.

bools.name: wemAboveSevereDmDamage
bools.comment: An overburdened character may, at the DM discretion, suffer damage.

bools.name: wemConsistentPathIsNormal
bools.comment: A well-kept path or roadway through topographically consistent normal or rugged terrain counts as normal terrain.

bools.name: wemPathInVRuggedIsRugged
bools.comment: A well-kept path or roadway through very rugged terrain counts as rugged.

bools.name: wemLargeScaleAssumesLightRugged
bools.comment: The large-scale scale assumes a lightly encumbered character moving over rugged terrain.

bools.name: wemT12ScaleForSlower
bools.comment: A slower base movement rate scales the Table 12 figures down accordingly.

bools.name: wemAccMoveNeedsRest
bools.comment: The accelerated rate requires periodic rests to avoid fatigue; the rest stops are built into the figures.

chains.name: wemStrRowFor
chains.comment: The plain-strength row dispatch for Table 11: 3 -> 0, 4-5 -> 1, 6-7 -> 2, 8-11 -> 3, 12-13 -> 4, 14-15 -> 5, 16 -> 6, 17 -> 7, 18 -> 8; a percentile strength reads the percentile rows instead (wemPctRowFor plus wemPctRowBase).

chains.name: wemPctRowFor
chains.comment: The percentile-row offset within Table 11: 18/01-50 -> 0, 18/51-75 -> 1, 18/76-90 -> 2, 18/91-99 -> 3, 18/00 (read the percentile as 100) -> 4.

The accelerated miles per half-day, normal terrain.

tables.audit_comment: the Table 12 grid: the encumbrance rows (none, light, moderate, heavy, severe) x the normal and accelerated rates over normal, rugged and very rugged terrain

examples.note: the worked example: a 12-inch rate covers 12 miles in the first half-day
the 1.5 miles per hour for any span under the half-day (3 miles every 2 hours)
the second eight hours at 3/4 rate: 9 miles
the light-encumbered, normal-terrain accelerated rate: 16 miles in the first eight hours
strength 8 reads the 8-11 row: the light band begins at 90 gp
the percentile 00 (read as 100) reads the 18/00 row: severe tops at 4500 gp
